messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm digging into some production anomalies where TTLs reported in metrics don't match eviction timestamps. Seems like we have TTL drift for prefixes that get rehydrated after demotion.
jon: Ugh. Observed anything that pins the TTL on read vs write?
kevin: Yeah, we do a shallow rehydrate that calls fetch_and_touch() which updates last_access but doesn't rewrite the original TTL. So metrics end up with original TTL but eviction logic uses a different clock.
anya: Can you paste the minimal stack of calls?
kevin: Sure — pseudo:
```
if (!present) {
  data = backend.fetch(prefix)
  cache.insert(prefix, data) // uses original ttl
} else {
  cache.touch(prefix) // extends lease but doesn't change ttl
}
```

sam: So we have two timers: lease/lease-heartbeat (for ownership) and ttl/expiry (for staleness). They drift because touch updates ownership but not expiry.
maria: Right. Problem shows up when a demoted prefix is rehydrated: it regains a lease (so it's not evicted immediately), metrics like "prefix_ttl_seconds" show original expiry which may already be stale. That leads ops to think we have healthy TTLs while evictions happen later.
jon: I think there are two orthogonal issues we should separate: 1) semantic correctness (do we want rehydrate to keep original expiry?) and 2) observability (are we exposing the right signals so ops can reason about drift).
anya: For semantics my vote: rehydrate should preserve TTL semantics from source of truth (i.e., backend). If backend says expiry=tsX then cache must reflect that expiry. Touch should not accidentally extend expiry unless the backend semantics allow it.
kevin: Agreed. But preserving backend expiry means we must fetch expiry metadata on rehydrate — currently fetch returns payload only. That implies a small API change to backend RPCs: return {value, expiry_ts} or at least TTL in seconds.
sam: Tradeoff: extra bytes and slightly more latency per fetch. But typical payloads are larger than a few bytes, so metadata is negligible. Operationally easier.
maria: Observability side: we should emit metric labels: eviction_reason={ttl, memory_pressure, manual}, observed_ttl_skew_seconds (gauge), and a histogram of time_between_rehydrate_and_eviction. Those will make it easy to detect systemic drift.
jon: Also add an event when rehydrate sees a backend expiry earlier than local expiry: rehydrate_ttl_override{prefix, old_expiry, new_expiry}. Could be emitted at info level.
kevin: Implementation plan suggestion: (1) extend PrefetchResponse to include expiry_ts (nullable), (2) on rehydrate, set local expiry = min(local_expiry, backend_expiry) if we want conservative correctness, or replace — we need to pick rule.
anya: I'd take replace to avoid complexity: cache should mirror backend semantics after rehydrate. If backend doesn't return expiry, fall back to previous behaviour but emit a metric.
sam: Replace is clearer. But check for races: if two nodes rehydrate and one has a slightly later backend expiry, we might override a more generous local expiry with an older one. However backend is authoritative.
maria: Good callouts. Races are fine because backend wins. We'll add an invariant test in the simulator: rehydrate must set expiry==backend_expiry when provided.
jon: On the observability front I'll add the following Prometheus metrics:
- prefix_evictions_total{reason}
- prefix_rehydrates_total
- prefix_ttl_skew_seconds (gauge): backend_expiry - local_expiry at time of rehydrate
- prefix_rehydrate_latency_seconds (histogram)
And logs for overrides.
kevin: For the API change we need backwards compatibility. We'll add expiry_ts optional field in the proto and default to omitted. Runtime will treat omitted as unknown — keep prior behaviour and emit metric 'rehydrate_missing_expiry_total'.
anya: Tests: unit for proto decoding, integration test that simulates demote->rehydrate with backend expiry mismatch, and a soak test to ensure no perf regressions.
maria: Action items:
- KEVIN: proto change + server-side code to return expiry (ticket INF-421)
- JON: add metrics and dashboards (INF-422)
- ANYA: write simulator test and invariant (INF-423)
- SAM: update rollout checklist + observability alerts (INF-424)
I'll queue infra PRs for canary after the proto change lands.
kevin: I'll prototype in a branch tonight. Won't be huge.
jon: One more UX question — should we expose TTL in the admin console per-prefix? Ops asked for a quick column.
maria: Yes, but only after metrics are reliable. Add column "expiry (backend)" and mark stale ones in red.
anya: Small note: this touches billing/reporting if we use TTL to estimate cache hit windows for cost attribution. Need finance FYI.
sam: I'll ping finance and include them on the ticket.
maria: Great. If nobody objects, I'll convert this thread into the RFC follow-up doc and link tickets. :+1:
kevin: No objections from me.
jon: LGTM
anya: LGTM
sre-bot: deploy-checklist: new metrics added -> ensure Prometheus retention configured.
